+# Code Review Report: QPB
+> Generated by [Quality Playbook](https://github.com/andrewstellman/quality-playbook) v1.5.6 — Andrew Stellman
+> Date: 2026-05-08 · Project: QPB
+
+## Pass 1: Structural Review
+
+Reviewed the Phase 3 scope named in `quality/RUN_CODE_REVIEW.md`: `bin/run_playbook.py`, `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py`, `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py`, `bin/run_state_lib.py`, `bin/archive_lib.py`, and `bin/role_map.py`.
+
+Resource lifecycle and state notes:
+- `bin/role_map.py:818-837` uses an atomic tempfile + `os.replace()` writeback and cleans up the temp file on failure. No leak or partial-write bug was confirmed there.
+- The reviewed slice is single-threaded; no true concurrent mutation was found. The relevant failure mode in this run is state-machine divergence between helper surfaces, not race conditions.
+
+#### `bin/run_playbook.py`
+- **Line 1568-1574:** `BUG` `docs_present()` checks only for any non-dot top-level file, so cite-only trees are missed and README/PDF-only trees are treated as docs-present. Expected: the startup warning helper uses the same recognized-docs predicate as the rest of the documentation-state logic. Actual: warning classification diverges from `_reference_docs_plaintext()`, `_evaluate_documentation_state()`, and `formal_docs_guard_banner()`. Why it matters: operator-visible startup messaging becomes self-contradictory.
+
+#### `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py`
+- **Line 90-93, 194-227, 263-276:** `BUG` Tier 4 ingest recurses nested non-`cite/` subdirectories and treats every non-`cite/` plaintext file as live context. Expected: only top-level plaintext files under `reference_docs/` become Tier 4 context unless the contract is widened. Actual: archived nested notes silently join the Phase 1 prompt budget. Why it matters: historical or out-of-scope docs can distort exploration results.
+
+#### `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py`
+- **Line 50-61:** `BUG` the bootstrap mirror creates `reference_docs/cite/` but never copies any source-side `docs_gathered/cite/*` files. Expected: both top-level and `cite/` placement are preserved. Actual: the helper iterates only the top level of `docs_gathered/`. Why it matters: self-audit runs can look docs-backed while silently losing the formal citation surface.
+
+#### `bin/run_state_lib.py`
+- **Line 171-198:** `BUG` the Phase 1 validator accepts long placeholders instead of the full written gate contract. Expected: the exact headings and analytical minima from the Phase 2 gate are enforced mechanically. Actual: only file existence, `>=120` lines, and a generic findings regex are checked. Why it matters: later phases can proceed on shallow exploration artifacts that should have been blocked.
+
+#### `bin/archive_lib.py`
+- **Line 69, 321-338:** `BUG` `_extract_bug_counts()` does not split on canonical titled headings. Expected: `### BUG-NNN: Title` sections contribute to severity totals. Actual: `_BUG_HEADING_PATTERN` matches only bare `### BUG-NNN`, so titled sections are skipped. Why it matters: archive metrics and index rendering undercount real bugs.
+
+#### `bin/role_map.py`
+- **Line 422-430, 455-468, 759-838:** no confirmed bug. `normalize_role_map_for_gate()` recomputes canonical `breakdown` and `summary`, and `validate_role_map()` then enforces the resulting shape. This satisfies the direct-vs-runner parity contract for the current code.
+- **Line 474-501:** no confirmed bug. `compute_breakdown()` keeps `playbook-output` in `other_share`, so historical `quality/` artifacts do not inflate `code_share`, `skill_share`, or `tool_share`.
+
+## Pass 2: Requirement Verification
+
+#### `REQ-001: Treat cite-only docs as docs-backed input`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574` — `docs_present()` scans only top-level files; `bin/run_playbook.py:1666-1669` treats `reference_docs/cite/` plaintext as docs-backed.  
+**Analysis**: the startup warning path still downgrades cite-only repos to docs-missing even though the canonical documentation-state helper accepts them.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-002: Use one recognized-docs predicate for warnings and state evaluation`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1572-1574` counts any non-dot top-level file; `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595` recognizes only `.md`/`.txt` and skips `README.md`.  
+**Analysis**: README-only, binary-only, and cite-only trees produce different answers depending on which helper surface is asked.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-003: Limit Tier 4 ingest to the documented reference-docs surface`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93`, `194-227`, `263-276` — the ingest path recurses the whole tree and returns every non-`cite/` plaintext record as Tier 4 context.  
+**Analysis**: nested non-`cite/` archives are not filtered out, so the code exceeds the documented surface.  
+**Severity**: `HIGH`
+
+#### `REQ-004: Preserve citable-vs-context placement during bootstrap mirroring`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61` — only top-level files are copied.  
+**Analysis**: the helper preserves top-level docs but drops the source-side `cite/` subtree entirely.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-005: Enforce the full Phase 1 exploration gate mechanically`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198` versus `SKILL.md:1260-1273`.  
+**Analysis**: the runtime validator enforces a much weaker contract than the skill's written Phase 2 gate.  
+**Severity**: `HIGH`
+
+#### `REQ-006: Parse canonical titled BUG headings in archive summaries`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/archive_lib.py:69` and `321-338` — the parser depends on a heading regex that omits `: Title`.  
+**Analysis**: canonical `BUGS.md` sections are invisible to archive severity counting.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-007: Normalize direct Phase 1 role maps before gate validation`
+**Status**: `SATISFIED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/role_map.py:759-838` recomputes `breakdown` and `summary`; `bin/role_map.py:422-430,455-468` validates the canonicalized result.  
+**Analysis**: a raw role map with `files[]` and `provenance` can be normalized into a gate-valid shape on the current code path.
+
+#### `REQ-008: Keep historical playbook output out of intrinsic surface accounting`
+**Status**: `SATISFIED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/role_map.py:162-169` defines the `playbook-output` role; `bin/role_map.py:474-501` buckets everything outside the skill/code/tool role sets into `other_share`.  
+**Analysis**: the accounting logic still isolates historical playbook output from intrinsic code and skill surface percentages.
+

+
+#### Shared Concept: `Documentation-state truth`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-001`, `REQ-002`  
+**What REQ-001 claims**: cite-only plaintext trees count as docs-backed input.  
+**What REQ-002 claims**: every startup surface shares one recognized-docs predicate.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1666-1669`  
+**Analysis**: the current code satisfies cite-only handling on the canonical documentation-state path but not on the warning path, which makes the two requirements fail together on the same helper drift.  
+**Impact**: operators can see a code-only warning on a run that the runner itself records as docs-backed.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Reference-doc surface integrity`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-003`, `REQ-004`  
+**What REQ-003 claims**: Tier 4 context is limited to the documented top-level reference-docs surface.  
+**What REQ-004 claims**: bootstrap mirroring preserves top-level-vs-`cite/` placement.  
+**Consistency**: `CONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93,194-227,263-276`, `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61`  
+**Analysis**: both requirements enforce boundary discipline around the same reference-docs tree. The current code violates both boundaries in opposite directions: one surface is too broad and the other is too narrow.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Phase-boundary integrity`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-005`, `REQ-007`  
+**What REQ-005 claims**: the exploration artifact must meet the full written Phase 1 gate before Phase 2 proceeds.  
+**What REQ-007 claims**: raw role maps are normalized into gate-ready shape before validation.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198`, `bin/role_map.py:759-838`  
+**Analysis**: role-map gate handling has already been hardened with runner-side normalization, but the exploration gate remains under-enforced.  
+**Impact**: one Phase 1 output is normalized into canonical shape automatically while another can remain structurally shallow and still pass.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Reporting accuracy under historical output pressure`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-006`, `REQ-008`  
+**What REQ-006 claims**: archive summaries preserve canonical bug counts.  
+**What REQ-008 claims**: accounting logic preserves intrinsic-surface counts under heavy historical output.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/archive_lib.py:69,321-338`, `bin/role_map.py:474-501`  
+**Analysis**: the role-map accounting logic correctly handles prior playbook output, but the archive bug counter still drops canonical titled entries.  
+**Impact**: historical-output-heavy repos can report accurate surface percentages while still undercounting confirmed bugs in archived summaries.

+# Confirmed Bugs: QPB
+> Generated by [Quality Playbook](https://github.com/andrewstellman/quality-playbook) v1.5.6 — Andrew Stellman
+> Date: 2026-05-08 · Project: QPB
+
+### BUG-001: `docs_present()` ignores cite-only docs-backed trees
+- Primary requirement: REQ-001
+- Severity: MEDIUM
+- Source: Code Review
+- File:line: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1661-1669`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1598-1621`
+- Covers: [REQ-001/cell-CITE_PLAINTEXT-STARTUP_WARNING]
+- Spec basis: `quality/REQUIREMENTS.md:13-24`
+- Expected behavior: a repo with only `reference_docs/cite/spec.md` is treated as docs-backed by every startup surface and does not trigger a code-only warning.
+- Actual behavior: `_evaluate_documentation_state()` and `formal_docs_guard_banner()` accept cite-only trees, but `docs_present()` only scans top-level files and returns `False`, so startup warning paths still treat the repo as code-only.
+- Regression test: `quality/test_regression.py::CodeReviewRegressionTests::test_bug_001_docs_present_recognizes_cite_only_docs`
+- Regression patch: `quality/patches/BUG-001-regression-test.patch`
+- Fix patch: `quality/patches/BUG-001-fix.patch`
+
+### BUG-002: `docs_present()` uses a broader predicate than the rest of the documentation-state logic
+- Primary requirement: REQ-002
+- Severity: MEDIUM
+- Source: Code Review
+- File:line: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1598-1621`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1661-1669`
+- Covers: [REQ-002/cell-README_ONLY-DOCS_PRESENT, REQ-002/cell-BINARY_ONLY-DOCS_PRESENT, REQ-002/cell-CITE_ONLY-DOCS_PRESENT]
+- Consolidation rationale: the same `docs_present()` loop causes all three misclassifications by treating any non-dot top-level file as documentation while ignoring cite-only trees.
+- Spec basis: `quality/REQUIREMENTS.md:26-38`
+- Expected behavior: README-only, binary-only, cite-only, and top-level plaintext trees are classified consistently across warnings, state evaluation, and the formal-doc banner.
+- Actual behavior: `docs_present()` counts `README.md` and `spec.pdf` as docs-present and misses cite-only trees, while the other two surfaces use `_reference_docs_plaintext()` and classify those same states differently.
+- Regression test: `quality/test_regression.py::CodeReviewRegressionTests::test_bug_002_docs_present_uses_the_recognized_plaintext_predicate`
+- Regression patch: `quality/patches/BUG-002-regression-test.patch`
+- Fix patch: `quality/patches/BUG-002-fix.patch`
+
+### BUG-003: Tier 4 ingest leaks nested non-`cite/` archives into Phase 1 context
+- Primary requirement: REQ-003
+- Severity: HIGH
+- Source: Code Review
+- File:line: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93`, `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:194-227`, `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:263-276`
+- Covers: [REQ-003/cell-TOP_LEVEL_PLAINTEXT_ONLY_FILTER-TIER4_CONTEXT]
+- Spec basis: `quality/REQUIREMENTS.md:40-51`
+- Expected behavior: Tier 4 ingest returns only top-level plaintext files from `reference_docs/`, while nested non-`cite/` archives stay out of the prompt budget.
+- Actual behavior: `_iter_candidates()` recurses the entire tree and `_collect()` marks every non-`cite/` plaintext file as Tier 4, so `load_tier4_context()` returns nested archival files like `reference_docs/nested/archive/notes.md`.

+## Pass 1: Structural Review
+
+Reviewed the Phase 3 scope named in `quality/RUN_CODE_REVIEW.md`: `bin/run_playbook.py`, `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py`, `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py`, `bin/run_state_lib.py`, `bin/archive_lib.py`, and `bin/role_map.py`.

+Resource lifecycle and state notes:
+- `bin/role_map.py:818-837` uses an atomic tempfile + `os.replace()` writeback and cleans up the temp file on failure. No leak or partial-write bug was confirmed there.
+- The reviewed slice is single-threaded; no true concurrent mutation was found. The relevant failure mode in this run is state-machine divergence between helper surfaces, not race conditions.
+
+#### `bin/run_playbook.py`
+- **Line 1568-1574:** `BUG` `docs_present()` checks only for any non-dot top-level file, so cite-only trees are missed and README/PDF-only trees are treated as docs-present. Expected: the startup warning helper uses the same recognized-docs predicate as the rest of the documentation-state logic. Actual: warning classification diverges from `_reference_docs_plaintext()`, `_evaluate_documentation_state()`, and `formal_docs_guard_banner()`. Why it matters: operator-visible startup messaging becomes self-contradictory.
+
+#### `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py`
+- **Line 90-93, 194-227, 263-276:** `BUG` Tier 4 ingest recurses nested non-`cite/` subdirectories and treats every non-`cite/` plaintext file as live context. Expected: only top-level plaintext files under `reference_docs/` become Tier 4 context unless the contract is widened. Actual: archived nested notes silently join the Phase 1 prompt budget. Why it matters: historical or out-of-scope docs can distort exploration results.
+
+#### `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py`
+- **Line 50-61:** `BUG` the bootstrap mirror creates `reference_docs/cite/` but never copies any source-side `docs_gathered/cite/*` files. Expected: both top-level and `cite/` placement are preserved. Actual: the helper iterates only the top level of `docs_gathered/`. Why it matters: self-audit runs can look docs-backed while silently losing the formal citation surface.
+
+#### `bin/run_state_lib.py`
+- **Line 171-198:** `BUG` the Phase 1 validator accepts long placeholders instead of the full written gate contract. Expected: the exact headings and analytical minima from the Phase 2 gate are enforced mechanically. Actual: only file existence, `>=120` lines, and a generic findings regex are checked. Why it matters: later phases can proceed on shallow exploration artifacts that should have been blocked.
+
+#### `bin/archive_lib.py`
+- **Line 69, 321-338:** `BUG` `_extract_bug_counts()` does not split on canonical titled headings. Expected: `### BUG-NNN: Title` sections contribute to severity totals. Actual: `_BUG_HEADING_PATTERN` matches only bare `### BUG-NNN`, so titled sections are skipped. Why it matters: archive metrics and index rendering undercount real bugs.
+
+#### `bin/role_map.py`
+- **Line 422-430, 455-468, 759-838:** no confirmed bug. `normalize_role_map_for_gate()` recomputes canonical `breakdown` and `summary`, and `validate_role_map()` then enforces the resulting shape. This satisfies the direct-vs-runner parity contract for the current code.
+- **Line 474-501:** no confirmed bug. `compute_breakdown()` keeps `playbook-output` in `other_share`, so historical `quality/` artifacts do not inflate `code_share`, `skill_share`, or `tool_share`.

+## Pass 2: Requirement Verification
+
+#### `REQ-001: Treat cite-only docs as docs-backed input`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574` — `docs_present()` scans only top-level files; `bin/run_playbook.py:1666-1669` treats `reference_docs/cite/` plaintext as docs-backed.  
+**Analysis**: the startup warning path still downgrades cite-only repos to docs-missing even though the canonical documentation-state helper accepts them.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-002: Use one recognized-docs predicate for warnings and state evaluation`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1572-1574` counts any non-dot top-level file; `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595` recognizes only `.md`/`.txt` and skips `README.md`.  
+**Analysis**: README-only, binary-only, and cite-only trees produce different answers depending on which helper surface is asked.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-003: Limit Tier 4 ingest to the documented reference-docs surface`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93`, `194-227`, `263-276` — the ingest path recurses the whole tree and returns every non-`cite/` plaintext record as Tier 4 context.  
+**Analysis**: nested non-`cite/` archives are not filtered out, so the code exceeds the documented surface.  
+**Severity**: `HIGH`
+
+#### `REQ-004: Preserve citable-vs-context placement during bootstrap mirroring`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61` — only top-level files are copied.  
+**Analysis**: the helper preserves top-level docs but drops the source-side `cite/` subtree entirely.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-005: Enforce the full Phase 1 exploration gate mechanically`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198` versus `SKILL.md:1260-1273`.  
+**Analysis**: the runtime validator enforces a much weaker contract than the skill's written Phase 2 gate.  
+**Severity**: `HIGH`
+
+#### `REQ-006: Parse canonical titled BUG headings in archive summaries`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/archive_lib.py:69` and `321-338` — the parser depends on a heading regex that omits `: Title`.  
+**Analysis**: canonical `BUGS.md` sections are invisible to archive severity counting.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-007: Normalize direct Phase 1 role maps before gate validation`
+**Status**: `SATISFIED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/role_map.py:759-838` recomputes `breakdown` and `summary`; `bin/role_map.py:422-430,455-468` validates the canonicalized result.  
+**Analysis**: a raw role map with `files[]` and `provenance` can be normalized into a gate-valid shape on the current code path.
+
+#### `REQ-008: Keep historical playbook output out of intrinsic surface accounting`
+**Status**: `SATISFIED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/role_map.py:162-169` defines the `playbook-output` role; `bin/role_map.py:474-501` buckets everything outside the skill/code/tool role sets into `other_share`.  
+**Analysis**: the accounting logic still isolates historical playbook output from intrinsic code and skill surface percentages.
+
+## Pass 3: Cross-Requirement Consistency
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Documentation-state truth`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-001`, `REQ-002`  
+**What REQ-001 claims**: cite-only plaintext trees count as docs-backed input.  
+**What REQ-002 claims**: every startup surface shares one recognized-docs predicate.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1666-1669`  
+**Analysis**: the current code satisfies cite-only handling on the canonical documentation-state path but not on the warning path, which makes the two requirements fail together on the same helper drift.  
+**Impact**: operators can see a code-only warning on a run that the runner itself records as docs-backed.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Reference-doc surface integrity`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-003`, `REQ-004`  
+**What REQ-003 claims**: Tier 4 context is limited to the documented top-level reference-docs surface.  
+**What REQ-004 claims**: bootstrap mirroring preserves top-level-vs-`cite/` placement.  
+**Consistency**: `CONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93,194-227,263-276`, `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61`  
+**Analysis**: both requirements enforce boundary discipline around the same reference-docs tree. The current code violates both boundaries in opposite directions: one surface is too broad and the other is too narrow.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Phase-boundary integrity`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-005`, `REQ-007`  
+**What REQ-005 claims**: the exploration artifact must meet the full written Phase 1 gate before Phase 2 proceeds.  
+**What REQ-007 claims**: raw role maps are normalized into gate-ready shape before validation.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198`, `bin/role_map.py:759-838`  
+**Analysis**: role-map gate handling has already been hardened with runner-side normalization, but the exploration gate remains under-enforced.  
+**Impact**: one Phase 1 output is normalized into canonical shape automatically while another can remain structurally shallow and still pass.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Reporting accuracy under historical output pressure`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-006`, `REQ-008`  
+**What REQ-006 claims**: archive summaries preserve canonical bug counts.  
+**What REQ-008 claims**: accounting logic preserves intrinsic-surface counts under heavy historical output.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/archive_lib.py:69,321-338`, `bin/role_map.py:474-501`  
+**Analysis**: the role-map accounting logic correctly handles prior playbook output, but the archive bug counter still drops canonical titled entries.  
+**Impact**: historical-output-heavy repos can report accurate surface percentages while still undercounting confirmed bugs in archived summaries.

+# Generated by Quality Playbook v1.5.6 — https://github.com/andrewstellman/quality-playbook
+# Author: Andrew Stellman · Date: 2026-05-08 · Project: QPB
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
+
+from bin import archive_lib, bootstrap_self_audit_docs as bootstrap_docs
+from bin import reference_docs_ingest as rdi
+from bin import run_playbook, run_state_lib
+
+try:
+    import pytest  # type: ignore
+except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - local fallback when only the unittest shim is available
+    pytest = None
+
+
+def xfail(*, reason: str) -> object:
+    if pytest is not None and hasattr(pytest, "mark") and hasattr(pytest.mark, "xfail"):
+        return pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=reason)
+    return unittest.expectedFailure
+
+
+def _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+class CodeReviewRegressionTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    @xfail(
+        reason=(
+            "BUG-001: docs_present() ignores cite-only docs-backed trees; "
+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-001-fix.patch"
+        )
+    )
+    def test_bug_001_docs_present_recognizes_cite_only_docs(self) -> None:
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            cite = repo / "reference_docs" / "cite"
+            cite.mkdir(parents=True)
+            (cite / "spec.md").write_text("# Spec\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self.assertTrue(run_playbook.docs_present(repo))
+
+    @xfail(
+        reason=(
+            "BUG-002: docs_present() counts README-only and binary-only trees as docs; "
+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-002-fix.patch"
+        )
+    )
+    def test_bug_002_docs_present_uses_the_recognized_plaintext_predicate(self) -> None:
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            refs = repo / "reference_docs"
+            refs.mkdir()
+            (refs / "README.md").write_text("ignored\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self.assertFalse(run_playbook.docs_present(repo))
+
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)

+- Severity: MEDIUM

+- Actual behavior: `_evaluate_documentation_state()` and `formal_docs_guard_banner()` accept cite-only trees, but `docs_present()` only scans top-level files and returns `False`, so startup warning paths still treat the repo as code-only.

+- Primary requirement: REQ-002

+- Source: Code Review

+- Consolidation rationale: the same `docs_present()` loop causes all three misclassifications by treating any non-dot top-level file as documentation while ignoring cite-only trees.
+- Spec basis: `quality/REQUIREMENTS.md:26-38`
+- Expected behavior: README-only, binary-only, cite-only, and top-level plaintext trees are classified consistently across warnings, state evaluation, and the formal-doc banner.
+- Actual behavior: `docs_present()` counts `README.md` and `spec.pdf` as docs-present and misses cite-only trees, while the other two surfaces use `_reference_docs_plaintext()` and classify those same states differently.
+- Regression test: `quality/test_regression.py::CodeReviewRegressionTests::test_bug_002_docs_present_uses_the_recognized_plaintext_predicate`

+# Code Review Report: QPB
+> Generated by [Quality Playbook](https://github.com/andrewstellman/quality-playbook) v1.5.6 — Andrew Stellman
+> Date: 2026-05-08 · Project: QPB
+
+## Pass 1: Structural Review
+
+Reviewed the Phase 3 scope named in `quality/RUN_CODE_REVIEW.md`: `bin/run_playbook.py`, `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py`, `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py`, `bin/run_state_lib.py`, `bin/archive_lib.py`, and `bin/role_map.py`.
+
+Resource lifecycle and state notes:
+- `bin/role_map.py:818-837` uses an atomic tempfile + `os.replace()` writeback and cleans up the temp file on failure. No leak or partial-write bug was confirmed there.
+- The reviewed slice is single-threaded; no true concurrent mutation was found. The relevant failure mode in this run is state-machine divergence between helper surfaces, not race conditions.
+
+#### `bin/run_playbook.py`
+- **Line 1568-1574:** `BUG` `docs_present()` checks only for any non-dot top-level file, so cite-only trees are missed and README/PDF-only trees are treated as docs-present. Expected: the startup warning helper uses the same recognized-docs predicate as the rest of the documentation-state logic. Actual: warning classification diverges from `_reference_docs_plaintext()`, `_evaluate_documentation_state()`, and `formal_docs_guard_banner()`. Why it matters: operator-visible startup messaging becomes self-contradictory.
+
+#### `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py`
+- **Line 90-93, 194-227, 263-276:** `BUG` Tier 4 ingest recurses nested non-`cite/` subdirectories and treats every non-`cite/` plaintext file as live context. Expected: only top-level plaintext files under `reference_docs/` become Tier 4 context unless the contract is widened. Actual: archived nested notes silently join the Phase 1 prompt budget. Why it matters: historical or out-of-scope docs can distort exploration results.
+
+#### `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py`
+- **Line 50-61:** `BUG` the bootstrap mirror creates `reference_docs/cite/` but never copies any source-side `docs_gathered/cite/*` files. Expected: both top-level and `cite/` placement are preserved. Actual: the helper iterates only the top level of `docs_gathered/`. Why it matters: self-audit runs can look docs-backed while silently losing the formal citation surface.
+
+#### `bin/run_state_lib.py`
+- **Line 171-198:** `BUG` the Phase 1 validator accepts long placeholders instead of the full written gate contract. Expected: the exact headings and analytical minima from the Phase 2 gate are enforced mechanically. Actual: only file existence, `>=120` lines, and a generic findings regex are checked. Why it matters: later phases can proceed on shallow exploration artifacts that should have been blocked.
+
+#### `bin/archive_lib.py`
+- **Line 69, 321-338:** `BUG` `_extract_bug_counts()` does not split on canonical titled headings. Expected: `### BUG-NNN: Title` sections contribute to severity totals. Actual: `_BUG_HEADING_PATTERN` matches only bare `### BUG-NNN`, so titled sections are skipped. Why it matters: archive metrics and index rendering undercount real bugs.
+
+#### `bin/role_map.py`
+- **Line 422-430, 455-468, 759-838:** no confirmed bug. `normalize_role_map_for_gate()` recomputes canonical `breakdown` and `summary`, and `validate_role_map()` then enforces the resulting shape. This satisfies the direct-vs-runner parity contract for the current code.
+- **Line 474-501:** no confirmed bug. `compute_breakdown()` keeps `playbook-output` in `other_share`, so historical `quality/` artifacts do not inflate `code_share`, `skill_share`, or `tool_share`.
+
+## Pass 2: Requirement Verification
+
+#### `REQ-001: Treat cite-only docs as docs-backed input`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574` — `docs_present()` scans only top-level files; `bin/run_playbook.py:1666-1669` treats `reference_docs/cite/` plaintext as docs-backed.  
+**Analysis**: the startup warning path still downgrades cite-only repos to docs-missing even though the canonical documentation-state helper accepts them.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-002: Use one recognized-docs predicate for warnings and state evaluation`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1572-1574` counts any non-dot top-level file; `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595` recognizes only `.md`/`.txt` and skips `README.md`.  
+**Analysis**: README-only, binary-only, and cite-only trees produce different answers depending on which helper surface is asked.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-003: Limit Tier 4 ingest to the documented reference-docs surface`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93`, `194-227`, `263-276` — the ingest path recurses the whole tree and returns every non-`cite/` plaintext record as Tier 4 context.  
+**Analysis**: nested non-`cite/` archives are not filtered out, so the code exceeds the documented surface.  
+**Severity**: `HIGH`
+
+#### `REQ-004: Preserve citable-vs-context placement during bootstrap mirroring`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61` — only top-level files are copied.  
+**Analysis**: the helper preserves top-level docs but drops the source-side `cite/` subtree entirely.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-005: Enforce the full Phase 1 exploration gate mechanically`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198` versus `SKILL.md:1260-1273`.  
+**Analysis**: the runtime validator enforces a much weaker contract than the skill's written Phase 2 gate.  
+**Severity**: `HIGH`
+
+#### `REQ-006: Parse canonical titled BUG headings in archive summaries`
+**Status**: `VIOLATED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/archive_lib.py:69` and `321-338` — the parser depends on a heading regex that omits `: Title`.  
+**Analysis**: canonical `BUGS.md` sections are invisible to archive severity counting.  
+**Severity**: `MEDIUM`
+
+#### `REQ-007: Normalize direct Phase 1 role maps before gate validation`
+**Status**: `SATISFIED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/role_map.py:759-838` recomputes `breakdown` and `summary`; `bin/role_map.py:422-430,455-468` validates the canonicalized result.  
+**Analysis**: a raw role map with `files[]` and `provenance` can be normalized into a gate-valid shape on the current code path.
+
+#### `REQ-008: Keep historical playbook output out of intrinsic surface accounting`
+**Status**: `SATISFIED`  
+**Evidence**: `bin/role_map.py:162-169` defines the `playbook-output` role; `bin/role_map.py:474-501` buckets everything outside the skill/code/tool role sets into `other_share`.  
+**Analysis**: the accounting logic still isolates historical playbook output from intrinsic code and skill surface percentages.
+

+

+**Requirements**: `REQ-001`, `REQ-002`  
+**What REQ-001 claims**: cite-only plaintext trees count as docs-backed input.  
+**What REQ-002 claims**: every startup surface shares one recognized-docs predicate.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1666-1669`  
+**Analysis**: the current code satisfies cite-only handling on the canonical documentation-state path but not on the warning path, which makes the two requirements fail together on the same helper drift.  
+**Impact**: operators can see a code-only warning on a run that the runner itself records as docs-backed.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Reference-doc surface integrity`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-003`, `REQ-004`  
+**What REQ-003 claims**: Tier 4 context is limited to the documented top-level reference-docs surface.  
+**What REQ-004 claims**: bootstrap mirroring preserves top-level-vs-`cite/` placement.  
+**Consistency**: `CONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93,194-227,263-276`, `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61`  
+**Analysis**: both requirements enforce boundary discipline around the same reference-docs tree. The current code violates both boundaries in opposite directions: one surface is too broad and the other is too narrow.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Phase-boundary integrity`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-005`, `REQ-007`  
+**What REQ-005 claims**: the exploration artifact must meet the full written Phase 1 gate before Phase 2 proceeds.  
+**What REQ-007 claims**: raw role maps are normalized into gate-ready shape before validation.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198`, `bin/role_map.py:759-838`  
+**Analysis**: role-map gate handling has already been hardened with runner-side normalization, but the exploration gate remains under-enforced.  
+**Impact**: one Phase 1 output is normalized into canonical shape automatically while another can remain structurally shallow and still pass.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Reporting accuracy under historical output pressure`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-006`, `REQ-008`  
+**What REQ-006 claims**: archive summaries preserve canonical bug counts.  
+**What REQ-008 claims**: accounting logic preserves intrinsic-surface counts under heavy historical output.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/archive_lib.py:69,321-338`, `bin/role_map.py:474-501`  
+**Analysis**: the role-map accounting logic correctly handles prior playbook output, but the archive bug counter still drops canonical titled entries.  
+**Impact**: historical-output-heavy repos can report accurate surface percentages while still undercounting confirmed bugs in archived summaries.

+from __future__ import annotations
+

+from pathlib import Path
+from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
+import unittest

+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

+    import pytest  # type: ignore
+except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - local fallback when only the unittest shim is available
+    pytest = None
+
+
+def xfail(*, reason: str) -> object:
+    if pytest is not None and hasattr(pytest, "mark") and hasattr(pytest.mark, "xfail"):
+        return pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=reason)
+    return unittest.expectedFailure
+
+
+def _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+class CodeReviewRegressionTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    @xfail(

+            "BUG-001: docs_present() ignores cite-only docs-backed trees; "
+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-001-fix.patch"
+        )
+    )
+    def test_bug_001_docs_present_recognizes_cite_only_docs(self) -> None:
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            cite = repo / "reference_docs" / "cite"
+            cite.mkdir(parents=True)
+            (cite / "spec.md").write_text("# Spec\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self.assertTrue(run_playbook.docs_present(repo))
+
+    @xfail(
+        reason=(
+            "BUG-002: docs_present() counts README-only and binary-only trees as docs; "
+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-002-fix.patch"
+        )
+    )
+    def test_bug_002_docs_present_uses_the_recognized_plaintext_predicate(self) -> None:
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            refs = repo / "reference_docs"
+            refs.mkdir()
+            (refs / "README.md").write_text("ignored\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self.assertFalse(run_playbook.docs_present(repo))
+
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            refs = repo / "reference_docs"
+            refs.mkdir()
+            (refs / "spec.pdf").write_bytes(b"%PDF-1.4\n")
+            self.assertFalse(run_playbook.docs_present(repo))
+
+    @xfail(
+        reason=(

+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-003-fix.patch"
+        )
+    )
+    def test_bug_003_tier4_context_excludes_nested_non_cite_archives(self) -> None:
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            refs = repo / "reference_docs"
+            (refs / "cite").mkdir(parents=True)
+            (refs / "top.md").write_text("top\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            (refs / "nested" / "archive").mkdir(parents=True)
+            (refs / "nested" / "archive" / "notes.md").write_text("nested\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self.assertEqual(rdi.load_tier4_context(repo), [("reference_docs/top.md", "top\n")])
+

+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-004-fix.patch"

+# Confirmed Bugs: QPB
+> Generated by [Quality Playbook](https://github.com/andrewstellman/quality-playbook) v1.5.6 — Andrew Stellman
+> Date: 2026-05-08 · Project: QPB
+
+### BUG-001: `docs_present()` ignores cite-only docs-backed trees
+- Primary requirement: REQ-001
+- Severity: MEDIUM
+- Source: Code Review
+- File:line: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1661-1669`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1598-1621`
+- Covers: [REQ-001/cell-CITE_PLAINTEXT-STARTUP_WARNING]
+- Spec basis: `quality/REQUIREMENTS.md:13-24`
+- Expected behavior: a repo with only `reference_docs/cite/spec.md` is treated as docs-backed by every startup surface and does not trigger a code-only warning.
+- Actual behavior: `_evaluate_documentation_state()` and `formal_docs_guard_banner()` accept cite-only trees, but `docs_present()` only scans top-level files and returns `False`, so startup warning paths still treat the repo as code-only.
+- Regression test: `quality/test_regression.py::CodeReviewRegressionTests::test_bug_001_docs_present_recognizes_cite_only_docs`
+- Regression patch: `quality/patches/BUG-001-regression-test.patch`
+- Fix patch: `quality/patches/BUG-001-fix.patch`
+
+### BUG-002: `docs_present()` uses a broader predicate than the rest of the documentation-state logic
+- Primary requirement: REQ-002
+- Severity: MEDIUM
+- Source: Code Review
+- File:line: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1598-1621`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1661-1669`
+- Covers: [REQ-002/cell-README_ONLY-DOCS_PRESENT, REQ-002/cell-BINARY_ONLY-DOCS_PRESENT, REQ-002/cell-CITE_ONLY-DOCS_PRESENT]
+- Consolidation rationale: the same `docs_present()` loop causes all three misclassifications by treating any non-dot top-level file as documentation while ignoring cite-only trees.
+- Spec basis: `quality/REQUIREMENTS.md:26-38`
+- Expected behavior: README-only, binary-only, cite-only, and top-level plaintext trees are classified consistently across warnings, state evaluation, and the formal-doc banner.
+- Actual behavior: `docs_present()` counts `README.md` and `spec.pdf` as docs-present and misses cite-only trees, while the other two surfaces use `_reference_docs_plaintext()` and classify those same states differently.
+- Regression test: `quality/test_regression.py::CodeReviewRegressionTests::test_bug_002_docs_present_uses_the_recognized_plaintext_predicate`
+- Regression patch: `quality/patches/BUG-002-regression-test.patch`
+- Fix patch: `quality/patches/BUG-002-fix.patch`
+
+### BUG-003: Tier 4 ingest leaks nested non-`cite/` archives into Phase 1 context
+- Primary requirement: REQ-003
+- Severity: HIGH
+- Source: Code Review
+- File:line: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93`, `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:194-227`, `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:263-276`
+- Covers: [REQ-003/cell-TOP_LEVEL_PLAINTEXT_ONLY_FILTER-TIER4_CONTEXT]
+- Spec basis: `quality/REQUIREMENTS.md:40-51`
+- Expected behavior: Tier 4 ingest returns only top-level plaintext files from `reference_docs/`, while nested non-`cite/` archives stay out of the prompt budget.
+- Actual behavior: `_iter_candidates()` recurses the entire tree and `_collect()` marks every non-`cite/` plaintext file as Tier 4, so `load_tier4_context()` returns nested archival files like `reference_docs/nested/archive/notes.md`.
+- Regression test: `quality/test_regression.py::CodeReviewRegressionTests::test_bug_003_tier4_context_excludes_nested_non_cite_archives`
+- Regression patch: `quality/patches/BUG-003-regression-test.patch`
+- Fix patch: `quality/patches/BUG-003-fix.patch`
+
+### BUG-004: Bootstrap mirroring drops the `cite/` formal-doc bucket
+- Primary requirement: REQ-004
+- Severity: MEDIUM
+- Source: Code Review
+- File:line: `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61`
+- Covers: [REQ-004/cell-CITE_FORMAL_DOCS-BOOTSTRAP_MIRROR]
+- Spec basis: `quality/REQUIREMENTS.md:53-64`
+- Expected behavior: `bin.bootstrap_self_audit_docs` mirrors both top-level context docs and `docs_gathered/cite/*` into `reference_docs/` with placement preserved.
+- Actual behavior: the helper creates `reference_docs/cite/` but iterates only the top level of `docs_gathered/`, so any source-side `cite/` files are silently omitted from the mirrored output.

+Reviewed the Phase 3 scope named in `quality/RUN_CODE_REVIEW.md`: `bin/run_playbook.py`, `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py`, `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py`, `bin/run_state_lib.py`, `bin/archive_lib.py`, and `bin/role_map.py`.

+- `bin/role_map.py:818-837` uses an atomic tempfile + `os.replace()` writeback and cleans up the temp file on failure. No leak or partial-write bug was confirmed there.
+- The reviewed slice is single-threaded; no true concurrent mutation was found. The relevant failure mode in this run is state-machine divergence between helper surfaces, not race conditions.
+
+#### `bin/run_playbook.py`
+- **Line 1568-1574:** `BUG` `docs_present()` checks only for any non-dot top-level file, so cite-only trees are missed and README/PDF-only trees are treated as docs-present. Expected: the startup warning helper uses the same recognized-docs predicate as the rest of the documentation-state logic. Actual: warning classification diverges from `_reference_docs_plaintext()`, `_evaluate_documentation_state()`, and `formal_docs_guard_banner()`. Why it matters: operator-visible startup messaging becomes self-contradictory.
+
+#### `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py`
+- **Line 90-93, 194-227, 263-276:** `BUG` Tier 4 ingest recurses nested non-`cite/` subdirectories and treats every non-`cite/` plaintext file as live context. Expected: only top-level plaintext files under `reference_docs/` become Tier 4 context unless the contract is widened. Actual: archived nested notes silently join the Phase 1 prompt budget. Why it matters: historical or out-of-scope docs can distort exploration results.
+
+#### `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py`
+- **Line 50-61:** `BUG` the bootstrap mirror creates `reference_docs/cite/` but never copies any source-side `docs_gathered/cite/*` files. Expected: both top-level and `cite/` placement are preserved. Actual: the helper iterates only the top level of `docs_gathered/`. Why it matters: self-audit runs can look docs-backed while silently losing the formal citation surface.
+
+#### `bin/run_state_lib.py`
+- **Line 171-198:** `BUG` the Phase 1 validator accepts long placeholders instead of the full written gate contract. Expected: the exact headings and analytical minima from the Phase 2 gate are enforced mechanically. Actual: only file existence, `>=120` lines, and a generic findings regex are checked. Why it matters: later phases can proceed on shallow exploration artifacts that should have been blocked.
+
+#### `bin/archive_lib.py`
+- **Line 69, 321-338:** `BUG` `_extract_bug_counts()` does not split on canonical titled headings. Expected: `### BUG-NNN: Title` sections contribute to severity totals. Actual: `_BUG_HEADING_PATTERN` matches only bare `### BUG-NNN`, so titled sections are skipped. Why it matters: archive metrics and index rendering undercount real bugs.
+
+#### `bin/role_map.py`
+- **Line 422-430, 455-468, 759-838:** no confirmed bug. `normalize_role_map_for_gate()` recomputes canonical `breakdown` and `summary`, and `validate_role_map()` then enforces the resulting shape. This satisfies the direct-vs-runner parity contract for the current code.
+- **Line 474-501:** no confirmed bug. `compute_breakdown()` keeps `playbook-output` in `other_share`, so historical `quality/` artifacts do not inflate `code_share`, `skill_share`, or `tool_share`.

+#### Shared Concept: `Documentation-state truth`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-001`, `REQ-002`  
+**What REQ-001 claims**: cite-only plaintext trees count as docs-backed input.  
+**What REQ-002 claims**: every startup surface shares one recognized-docs predicate.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595`, `bin/run_playbook.py:1666-1669`  
+**Analysis**: the current code satisfies cite-only handling on the canonical documentation-state path but not on the warning path, which makes the two requirements fail together on the same helper drift.  
+**Impact**: operators can see a code-only warning on a run that the runner itself records as docs-backed.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Reference-doc surface integrity`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-003`, `REQ-004`  
+**What REQ-003 claims**: Tier 4 context is limited to the documented top-level reference-docs surface.  
+**What REQ-004 claims**: bootstrap mirroring preserves top-level-vs-`cite/` placement.  
+**Consistency**: `CONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93,194-227,263-276`, `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61`  
+**Analysis**: both requirements enforce boundary discipline around the same reference-docs tree. The current code violates both boundaries in opposite directions: one surface is too broad and the other is too narrow.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Phase-boundary integrity`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-005`, `REQ-007`  
+**What REQ-005 claims**: the exploration artifact must meet the full written Phase 1 gate before Phase 2 proceeds.  
+**What REQ-007 claims**: raw role maps are normalized into gate-ready shape before validation.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198`, `bin/role_map.py:759-838`  
+**Analysis**: role-map gate handling has already been hardened with runner-side normalization, but the exploration gate remains under-enforced.  
+**Impact**: one Phase 1 output is normalized into canonical shape automatically while another can remain structurally shallow and still pass.
+
+#### Shared Concept: `Reporting accuracy under historical output pressure`
+**Requirements**: `REQ-006`, `REQ-008`  
+**What REQ-006 claims**: archive summaries preserve canonical bug counts.  
+**What REQ-008 claims**: accounting logic preserves intrinsic-surface counts under heavy historical output.  
+**Consistency**: `INCONSISTENT`  
+**Code evidence**: `bin/archive_lib.py:69,321-338`, `bin/role_map.py:474-501`  
+**Analysis**: the role-map accounting logic correctly handles prior playbook output, but the archive bug counter still drops canonical titled entries.  
+**Impact**: historical-output-heavy repos can report accurate surface percentages while still undercounting confirmed bugs in archived summaries.

+# Generated by Quality Playbook v1.5.6 — https://github.com/andrewstellman/quality-playbook
+# Author: Andrew Stellman · Date: 2026-05-08 · Project: QPB
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
+
+from bin import archive_lib, bootstrap_self_audit_docs as bootstrap_docs
+from bin import reference_docs_ingest as rdi
+from bin import run_playbook, run_state_lib
+
+try:
+    import pytest  # type: ignore
+except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - local fallback when only the unittest shim is available
+    pytest = None
+
+
+def xfail(*, reason: str) -> object:
+    if pytest is not None and hasattr(pytest, "mark") and hasattr(pytest.mark, "xfail"):
+        return pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=reason)
+    return unittest.expectedFailure
+
+
+def _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+class CodeReviewRegressionTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    @xfail(
+        reason=(
+            "BUG-001: docs_present() ignores cite-only docs-backed trees; "
+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-001-fix.patch"
+        )
+    )
+    def test_bug_001_docs_present_recognizes_cite_only_docs(self) -> None:
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            cite = repo / "reference_docs" / "cite"
+            cite.mkdir(parents=True)
+            (cite / "spec.md").write_text("# Spec\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self.assertTrue(run_playbook.docs_present(repo))
+
+    @xfail(
+        reason=(
+            "BUG-002: docs_present() counts README-only and binary-only trees as docs; "
+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-002-fix.patch"
+        )
+    )
+    def test_bug_002_docs_present_uses_the_recognized_plaintext_predicate(self) -> None:
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            refs = repo / "reference_docs"
+            refs.mkdir()
+            (refs / "README.md").write_text("ignored\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self.assertFalse(run_playbook.docs_present(repo))
+
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            refs = repo / "reference_docs"
+            refs.mkdir()
+            (refs / "spec.pdf").write_bytes(b"%PDF-1.4\n")
+            self.assertFalse(run_playbook.docs_present(repo))
+
+    @xfail(
+        reason=(
+            "BUG-003: load_tier4_context() ingests nested non-cite archives; "
+            "remove after applying quality/patches/BUG-003-fix.patch"
+        )
+    )
+    def test_bug_003_tier4_context_excludes_nested_non_cite_archives(self) -> None:
+        with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = Path(tmp)
+            refs = repo / "reference_docs"
+            (refs / "cite").mkdir(parents=True)
+            (refs / "top.md").write_text("top\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            (refs / "nested" / "archive").mkdir(parents=True)
+            (refs / "nested" / "archive" / "notes.md").write_text("nested\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self.assertEqual(rdi.load_tier4_context(repo), [("reference_docs/top.md", "top\n")])
+
+    @xfail(
